sophia: Heads-up: Asterion reported weird rounding/format changes after we merged their LoRA adapter (ast-lora-v1) and ran int4. They see amounts rounded to nearest 100 in some outputs. Can someone run a quick compatibility + int4 smoke? short evalpack (25 examples) attached in ticket.

lee: I can take this. Do we have the specific examples that failed? ticket says CSV export + invoice renderer. :csv:

sophia: paste of flagged examples: 
- $2,500.00
- 2.500,00 .00 €
- ¥1,200
- Total: 2500
They said the model started outputting "2,000" instead of "2,500" for some templates after quantized merge.

omar: queued a quick job on host-shadow with quant=int4 and adapter ast-lora-v1. Using rdx-medium-3b for speed. eval id eva-1759998889-a.

qa-bot: job eva-1759998889-a started on runner-7. est runtime ~4m.

omar: command run: 
```
redwood eval run --model rdx-medium-3b --adapter ast-lora-v1 --quant int4 --tasks numeric-formatting,csv-emit --samples 25 --out /tmp/asterion-smoke.json
```

omar: quick stats: base PPL=9.8, merged PPL=10.6 (+8.2%). Failures: 4/25 numeric mismatch (rounding to hundreds), 2/25 token boundary changes on thousands separator. One example where "2500" -> "2000" predicted token sequence.

lee: weird. Could be an attention/precision issue after quantization causing softmax shifts. Any evidence of catastrophic bias?

omar: looked at logits for that example: top tokens shifted but not extreme. Attn head patterns look ok. However adapter's bias terms have some >2.0 magnitude on a few heads after merge. Might indicate overfit on training examples with coarse rounding.

sophia: actionables: 1) request training seed set from Asterion (they may have trained with integer-rounded dataset); 2) run same eval with quant=int8 to isolate quantization impact; 3) add failing examples to onboarding regression set and tag release.

lee: re-run with int8: PPL(merged, int8)=10.0, delta +2.0% vs base. Numeric mismatches reduced to 1/25. So quant is amplifying the issue.

omar: tried a quick weight-clamp merge (clip adapter deltas to [-0.5,0.5]) and reran int4 smoke locally: mismatches dropped to 0/25, PPL up slightly but acceptable. I put the temp merge script here: https://gist.github.com/temp/astar-weight-clamp

qa-bot: note: added the 4 flagged examples to onboarding-regress/asterion.json with label "currency-rounding".

sophia: good. We'll share the clamp workaround and recommend retraining with mix of precise amounts and locale variants. Also ask SE to confirm whether Asterion used any postprocessing that truncates decimals server-side.

lee: FYI, I also tried token-remap that normalizes thousands separators to comma before tokenization; reduced token-boundary diffs but rounding mismatches persisted. So two orthogonal fixes: tokenizer remap for separators, and weight clamp / data fix for rounding bias.

omar: I'll draft a short runbook: steps to triage numeric regressions on adapter merges (check training data for rounding, run int8 v int4, inspect adapter delta magnitude, try clamp merge, add examples to regress suite).

sophia: please assign runbook to eng-ml/runs and ping SE to request training artifacts from customer. cc @support-ops.

ingest-bot: ticket 43219 updated: requested training seeds from customer Asterion.

sophia: marking this thread as "smoke->investigating". I'll follow up when customer responds. Thanks all :pray:
